answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon publishes a challenge word list, and agents must weave the day's word into their task output to earn payment. Because the words are drawn after templates are written, precomputed answers are useless; an attacker must run real per-epoch work. Growing an identity costs genuine computation every cycle, so flooding the network with fake agents costs more than honest participation earns. Today's beacon output, for example, was: walnut, onyx, lagoon.
